correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, each external neighbor count of a subset described by indices X and Y equals |Y|-1_{i in Y} or |X|-1_{j in X}. If an inclusion-minimal fort contains three members of a side it is exactly that pure triple. For both side occupancies at most two, a size-two occupancy forces equality of both index pairs, leaving precisely matched quartets. Cases with no side size two and fewer than three in all cannot form a fort. All these candidates meet the external-neighbor test. A stalled white set is a fort, so every zero forcing set is exactly a transversal of these minimal forts. This gives the all-set generating polynomial by counting omitted vertices with each side at most two, subtracting matching size-two omitted pairs. The LP lower bound follows by summing all within-side triple inequalities; uniform 1/3 is feasible. Equality uniquely fixes weights for n>=4. Each disjoint fort uses at least three vertices; packing by pure triples plus a quartet for the n congruent 2 case attains floor(2n/3). Verified by standalone direct forcing simulation and independent graph-adjacency fort checks for finite stated ranges; no finite check was substituted for universal proof.

originality.rationale: Accessible published mathematical records were searched for crown graph, K_{n,n} minus perfect matching, direct product K_2 × K_n, minimal forts, zero forcing polynomial and fractional forcing aliases. Full primary texts in arXiv:2310.17904, arXiv:2404.05963 and arXiv:2202.04997 were compared at the level of exact object and implication. The prior generalized fort/LP and maximal failed principles are acknowledged, but they do not supply the explicit complete crown-graph minimal-fort hypergraph and induced closed polynomial/packing/fractional spectrum. Crown graphs are outside the complete multipartite minimal-fort hypotheses; the products paper does not study direct products. Residual risk from unindexed, differently named literature remains.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact solution of the complete standard zero forcing and fort-obstruction problem for the canonical matching-deleted complete bipartite family, not merely a recalculation of its scalar forcing number. Classifying every minimal obstruction yields the complete forcing polynomial, all maximal failed configurations, all integer disjoint-fort packings, the fractional transversal minimum and uniqueness of the fractional optimizer for n>=4. The extremal ratio tends to three, a structurally motivated limit with potential usefulness for testing integral versus fractional fort formulations. The counting and LP claims have an infinite parameter and clear graph-theoretic motivation.
